source_excerpt:
An open-source proactive agent that gets your work done and keeps you in the loop
Built on OpenBot and CopilotKit · Quick start · Overview · Features and Capabilities · How it works · Contributing
Each agent has a computer of its own. Use it on the web, on mobile, in Slack, or in Microsoft Teams.
Host OpenDuet yourself and choose your own model. Requires a free CopilotKit Intelligence project for threads and memory. Everything that makes it OpenDuet lives in one folder , so copy it and make it your own.
Building on OpenDuet? Talk to a CopilotKit engineer →
Setting it up takes a minute: onboarding ends on a checklist of what OpenDuet depends on.
OpenDuet does not wait to be asked. It starts your day with a short brief, keeps working on a computer of its own while you step away, and comes back only when something needs you. Before it sends, pays, signs, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it is about to do and waits for your answer.
Early, and in active development. OpenDuet runs today as OpenBot , CopilotKit's open-source, self-hosted agent platform, with OpenDuet's name, Bots and skills on top. It already reads your Gmail and calendar, sorts what needs you from what can wait, and makes the morning brief. Features and Capabilities lists what works today. Expect things to move. Issues and ideas are welcome.
A morning brief. One short message to start the day: what is on, what changed, and what needs a decision from you.
What needs you, and what can wait. It looks across your mail, calendar, and Slack, brings the few things that need you to the top, and holds the rest until they matter.
Keeps working when you step away. Hand it a task and it carries on in a computer of its own: a real browser, its own files, and only the tools you grant. It tells you when it is done, or when it is stuck.
Asks before it acts. Sending a message, making a payment, signing a document, deleting anything: it shows you the exact action and waits. Allow once, always allow, or refuse.
Never sees your passwords. When a site needs a login, you type it into a masked box. The password reaches the site, never the conversation the agent reads.
Checks what leaves. Every outgoing message is checked for sensitive information, so a card number or a health detail does not go out by accident.
Yours to run. Self-host it, choose your own model, and keep your data in your own database.
See Features and Capabilities for what works today.
Everything below works today when you run this repository.
You will need Docker, Bun 1.3 or newer, Node (for npx , which runs the CopilotKit CLI), a model key, and a CopilotKit Intelligence project. Intelligence is required : it keeps OpenDuet's threads and memory, and the server will not start without its key. The free Developer plan is enough.
Run every command in this section from the repository root.
Sign in and pick an Intelligence project:
project select writes the project's key to .env as CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY , its telemetry ID as CPK_TELEMETRY_ID , and your choice to .copilotkit/project.json . The server reads INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY , not CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY , so the last command finishes the job. It makes sure the project has an openbot Learning container, creating one if it does not (see Automatic Learning ), then copies the key to INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY and sets CPK_INTELLIGENCE_LEARNING_CONTAINER_ID=openbot . It reads .env and .copilotkit/ from the directory it runs in, which is why it runs here and not from openbot/ . If .env already has an INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY , it keeps it and only checks that the container exists.
Put your model key in .env . The OpenDuet Bot runs OpenAI's gpt-5.6-terra , set in openbot/examples/openduet/model.yaml , so by default that is:
Another OpenAI model. Change default_model in openbot/examples/openduet/model.yaml , or in your copy of it (see Make it your own ). BOT_MODEL does not change an OpenAI model on its own. It is used only when OPENAI_BASE_URL is also set to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and then it names the model that endpoint serves.
Anthropic. Set BOT_PROVIDER=anthropic and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... . The model is BOT_MODEL if you set one, such as BOT_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 , and claude-sonnet-4-5 if you do not.
Set these before you start it. Settings → Setup in the app says whether the model key works.
and open http://localhost:3010 . The script starts Postgres and each Bot's computer in Docker, applies the database migrations, and starts the API server, the routine worker, and the app. It checks that each one answers before it prints the next steps. bash scripts/stop.sh stops the app, the worker, the API server and the Docker services, and removes the Bot computers that belong to this install, the ones with its COMPUTER_NAMESPACE . It does not touch another install's. The database, each Bot's files and its browser profile are Docker volumes, so they stay. Add --keep-computers to leave the Bot computers running.
If port 5432 is already taken on your machine, set POSTGRES_PORT in .env to a free port and change the port in DATABASE_URL to match.
For a shared Bot computer, set OPENBOT_ONE_COMPUTER_EACH=false , leave COMPUTER_SUPERVISOR_URL empty, and point AGENT_COMPUTER_URL at http://localhost: (4100 by default). The API and the agent-computer Compose service must use the same nonempty COMPUTER_TOKEN . Start through bash scripts/start.sh to keep them in agreement; it writes the resolved token into .env so a later direct Bun restart keeps it. If you change the token, rerun the start script and restart any API processes launched manually. For a computer per Bot, keep OPENBOT_ONE_COMPUTER_EACH=true : the supervisor owns those containers and their assigned ports; do not point AGENT_COMPUTER_URL at a remembered random port.
To run a second install beside another on one machine, give it its own COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME , COMPUTER_NAMESPACE , image tags ( COMPUTER_IMAGE and the other *_IMAGE settings), and a value for every *_PORT . Change the addresses built from those ports to match: DATABASE_URL , AGENT_COMPUTER_URL , MANAGED_AGENT_AG_UI_URL , OPENBOT_PUBLIC_URL and TRUSTED_ORIGINS . If both use the same Intelligence project, give it its own DEPLOYMENT_ID too. openbot/docs/configuration.md lists them. Two installs can instead share one computer, if they use the same token.
To diagnose a 401, inspect container names and port mappings with docker ps , then compare COMPUTER_TOKEN by equality without printing either value. The setup checklist authenticates against the provider and checks network-policy delivery; a configured URL alone no longer means Ready. A sleeping computer reads Not checked until it is running and Check again succeeds.
The CopilotKit runtime sends usage telemetry to CopilotKit, tagged OpenDuet. Set COPILOTKIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 to turn it off. What is sent .
Once it is running, try the parts that work today:
Ask the OpenDuet Bot to do something in its own browser, and watch it work on its computer.
Choose what it must ask you about first in /settings/approvals .
Ask it to do something on a schedule. You will find it in /routines .
Sign-in for a team, and Slack and Teams, are OpenBot's: see openbot/docs . A hosted or deploy guide for OpenDuet is not published yet, and neither is an OpenDuet image, so the Quick start above is the supported way to run it today. The Docker and Helm guides in openbot/docs deploy plain OpenBot from OpenBot's own image, not OpenDuet.
Gmail and Calendar need a Google OAuth client, which an administrator registers once. Each person then connects their own account under Connections . With the default .env you are the administrator. Settings → Setup in the app shows which of these steps is still open and links to each page. openbot/docs/plugins/google-workspace.md has the Google Cloud steps: the two APIs to enable, the consent screen, and the OAuth client.
Connecting needs OPENBOT_PUBLIC_URL , the API's address that Google sends people back to. .env.example sets it to http://localhost:3001 , so it has to change if you move SERVER_PORT , and it must be the public address once deployed.
To try it without a Google account, use the fake Google that ships for tests and demos. Setting its URL is not enough on its own. The steps are:
Start the fake Google. It serves an invented inbox and calendar. bun openbot/scripts/fake-google/server.ts --port 4900
Start the fake Google. It serves an invented inbox and calendar.
In .env , set OPENDUET_FAKE_GOOGLE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4900 , then start OpenDuet. If it is already running, run bash scripts/stop.sh and bash scripts/start.sh , because the API reads .env only when it starts.
In .env , set OPENDUET_FAKE_GOOGLE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4900 , then start OpenDuet. If it is already running, run bash scripts/stop.sh and bash scripts/start.sh , because the API reads .env only when it starts.
Open /admin/plugins/google-workspace . Turn on Enable for this deployment , open OAuth client and paste any client ID and secret (the fake accepts anything), then press Refresh tools .
Open /admin/plugins/google-workspace . Turn on Enable for this deployment , open OAuth client and paste any client ID and secret (the fake accepts anything), then press Refresh tools .
Grant the connector's tools to the OpenDuet Bot at /admin/plugins/google-workspace/bots/openduet .
Grant the connector's tools to the OpenDuet Bot at /admin/plugins/google-workspace/bots/openduet .
Open /connections/google-workspace and press Connect . The fake consents at once, as maya@marlowceramics.com , and sends you straight back.
Open /connections/google-workspace and press Connect . The fake consents at once, as maya@marlowceramics.com , and sends you straight back.
OPENBOT_PUBLIC_URL has to match the API's port, because the fake sends you back through it. curl http://127.0.0.1:4900/__fake/sent shows anything OpenDuet sent. The variable is ignored when NODE_ENV=production . To switch to real Google, remove it, restart, and connect again: the stored sign-in belongs to the fake.
The OpenDuet Bot ships with a public-web research skill. Set up a research provider to let it find sources and read pages without using its browser. The catalogue includes Parallel, Exa and Firecrawl. An administrator enables a connector and grants its search and fetch tools after reviewing the guide's controls and data-sharing risks.
Then try /research-public-web with a request such as “Compare three public project-management tools for a small team, check their current pricing, and make a brief with source links.”
OpenDuet is meant to be copied. Everything that makes it OpenDuet rather than OpenBot is in openbot/examples/openduet :
Copy the folder, change it, and point TENANT_PACKAGE_DIR in .env at your copy (relative to openbot/server ). OpenBot's code underneath stays as it is in openbot/ , so OpenBot's fixes can still be brought in.
OpenDuet is built on top of OpenBot , CopilotKit's open-source, self-hosted agent platform. OpenBot provides the server, the app, each Bot's computer, the approval boundary, the audit trail, sign-in, and the Slack and Teams channels. OpenDuet adds the morning brief, Tasks, Make and its own Bots and skills on top; its name, Bots and skills live in one folder, openbot/examples/openduet . To build a different assistant on the same foundation, start from OpenBot , or read more at copilotkit.ai/openbot .
Everything below works in this repository today.
Channels. You reach OpenDuet where you already are: the web app, Slack, or Microsoft Teams, all of which OpenBot supports today.
Server. OpenBot's server hosts the CopilotKit runtime and sends each turn to the agent over AG-UI . OpenDuet adds two pieces in front of it: a triage step that decides what needs you and what can wait, and a morning brief built from it. Both build on OpenBot's routines, which give an agent scheduled turns that run as you.
Agent. Any endpoint that speaks AG-UI can be the agent, whether it is built with LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, Google ADK, or written by hand. OpenDuet is not tied to one framework or one model.
Its own computer. Each agent gets a container of its own, with Chromium, a /workspace volume, a browser profile, and a shell. That is where it keeps working while you step away. When it hits a login wall or a two-factor prompt, it asks for help and you can take the wheel.
Approvals. Every action the agent takes goes through one gateway. The gateway checks the action against your policy, writes an audit record, and only then acts. Actions set to ask pause and show you the exact action and the rule that asked, with Allow once , Always allow , and Refuse . Deny rules refuse an action outright. OpenDuet's defaults will ask before anything that sends, pays, signs, or deletes.
Passwords and credentials. When a site needs a secret, the agent asks for it through a masked box. The value goes to the site; the transcript records only that a secret was requested. Credentials you store are encrypted at rest, write-only, never returned by an API, and redacted from audit events.
What leaves. OpenBot treats any tool it cannot positively classify as a read as a write, and redacts secrets from its audit trail. A message to other people always asks first, showing who it goes to and what it says.
Memory. Threads and memory live in CopilotKit Intelligence , so conversations survive restarts and what it has learned about you carries over. You can see what it remembers about you, and tell it facts directly.
Skills and connectors. Skills are instructions you write once and call with / . Connected apps are governed MCP servers: Google Drive and Notion ship in OpenBot's catalogue, and Composio brokers more. A connector is granted to an agent before it can be used.
OpenDuet is early, so please open an issue before starting substantial work. Much of the foundation lives in OpenBot : changes to the computer, the gateway, approvals, credentials, or connectors usually belong there.
OpenDuet is built and maintained by CopilotKit , the team behind OpenBot and the AG-UI protocol .
It is CopilotKit's open-source take on the proactive-agent category: assistants that reach out first, such as Claude Duet. OpenDuet is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
